The study included 99 patients with PET-positive local recurrence after radical prostatectomy.
Patients were treated with intensity-modulated salvage radiotherapy (sRT) guided by PSMA-PET/CT.
Radiomic features were extracted from CT images using volumes of interest defined by PSMA-PET uptakes.
The radiomic model outperformed clinical and combined clinical-radiomic models in predicting BCR.
The C-index for the radiomic model was 0.71 in the test set.
The C-index for the clinical model was 0.53 in the test set.
The C-index for the combined clinical-radiomic model was 0.63 in the test set.
The radiomic model achieved significantly improved patient stratification in Kaplan-Meier analysis (p < 0.001).
The time-dependent net reclassification improvement (tdNRI) was 0.392 for the radiomic model and 0.762 for the combined model.
The AUC of the radiomic signature at 24 months follow-up was 0.73.
The most predictive radiomic feature was 'firstorder_mean' (mean CT intensity).
The optimal cut-off value for mean CT intensity was 19.7 Hounsfield units (HU).
The median follow-up time was 29 months (range 3–79 months).
The study used nested cross-validation with 10 iterations of 5-fold cross-validation.
Feature reduction methods included mrmr, spearman, concordance, mifs, and random selection.
The clinical model included age, ISUP grade, initial PSA, maximum PSA prior to sRT, and rcN-status.
The combined model included both clinical and radiomic features.
The radiomic model showed durable prediction of BCR-free survival in time-dependent ROC analysis.
The decision curve analysis demonstrated a higher clinical net benefit for the radiomic model.
The combined model showed higher sensitivity improvement (0.78) compared to the radiomic model alone (0.26).
The most frequently selected clinical feature was 'initial PSA'.
The primary endpoint was BCR-free survival (BRFS).
No patient died during the follow-up period.
The study was conducted at three high-volume centers in Germany.
The study was retrospective and multicenter.
